735	| Brandt 2024 (TCC) MKtP diagonalisation → π(x) mod 2 lower bound (FOCUS-3) | FAIL | E | Brandt 2024 "Lower Bounds for Levin-Kolmogorov Complexity" (TCC, IACR ePrint 2024/687) proves MKtP ∉ DTIME[O(n)] unconditionally (Thm 1) plus three sharper conditional results (Thm 2 one-sided heuristic; Cor 1 quadratic for RAM; Cor 2 slightly super-linear) via a length-monotonic depth-first traversal TRAVERSE_{c_Ω,c_Kt} that uses 1-Kt-randomness of Chaitin's Ω prefixes to bypass the black-box barrier. The technique relativizes and is **not subject to algebrization or Natural Proofs (T4)**, satisfying FOCUS-3's stated promise. **HOWEVER it does not extend to π(x) mod 2** for four orthogonal reasons: (O1) the hard string z that TRAVERSE produces is an oracle-dependent Kt-random prefix, NOT a fixed natural function — π_N is fixed per N and Brandt has no mechanism to use a "fast π-decider" to construct z; (O2) the contradiction is `Kt(z) ≥ |z|` ∧ `Kt(z) ≤ |M| + log₂ t` — self-referential Kt on both sides — and there is no analog of `f-hardness(z) ≥ |z|` for a fixed Boolean function f = π mod 2; (O3) Lemma 2's 1-Kt-randomness of Ω prefixes is the *only* black-box-barrier-bypass ingredient, and there is no density of "π-hard inputs" (π is total and in DTIME[x^{2/3}]); (O4) Brandt produces UNIFORM-TIME lower bounds, not circuit lower bounds — Chain E (E5.3) needs a circuit lower bound and Brandt explicitly avoids the Williams/Hirahara algorithmic-method route precisely because that's the route subject to Natural Proofs on stronger classes. Empirical pseudorandomness of π(x) mod 2 (E1.9, 33 measures, novel/pseudorandomness_of_pi.md) is consistent with π_N being Kt-random but does not establish it asymptotically and would itself face T4. Bounded-Kt simulator (3-bit-op stack VM, L_MAX=12, T_MAX=4096) confirms TRAVERSE behaves as in the paper (descends on Kt-random, right-steps on compressible) and that π_N is incompressible by short bounded-VM programs at all tested N ∈ {3..10}. Cumulative effect: with E7.10 (AKS modulus-twist orthogonality, S61/S64/S66) closing the AKS family and this closure ruling out Brandt-class diagonalisation-via-meta-complexity, **Chain E is now closed for both known technique families**; only an entirely-new lower-bound technique or a non-AKS TC⁰ primality test remains. Suggested EDGE: E5.8 — Brandt 2024 is structurally welded to MKtP. Cites E5.3, E5.5, E1.9, E7.10, T4. See experiments/constructions/brandt_mktp/. | 51 |

Sophie-Germain sub-class (p=2q+1, q prime, N=670): mean/std within single sigma of others, KS p=0.947. Extrapolated to x=10⁶: error 93.27, relative 0.1% — absolute error scales as **√x exactly tracking li(x) − π(x)** (the standard prime-counting error term, RH-bounded O(√x log x)). The "winner" is a refined-li approximant, not a structural det representation. Upper-decade exponent (n ∈ [556, 12715]) of residual RMS scales as `RMS ~ n^{0.605}` — **at or above** the √n chaos baseline of δ(n) directly. Halving propagates, not shrinks, the chaotic component. **Independence-of-scales structural argument** (sharper than line 338): theta(n) = (R^{-1}(n) − 2 R^{-1}(n/2)) + (δ(n) − 2 δ(n/2)). First bracket is polylog-smooth. Second bracket is sum of two *independent* chaotic signals because δ(n) and δ(n/2) sample different ranges of zeta zeros (heights ~√n vs ~√(n/2)); independent chaotic signals add in RMS, not cancel: Var[δ(n) − 2δ(n/2)] = Var[δ(n)] + 4·Var[δ(n/2)] ~ const·n. Strong family-level corollary: any polylog-many evaluations of p at inputs n_1,…,n_k ≪ n cannot reconstruct p(n), because they don't carry zero-phase data at height √n — only low-frequency phase. See experiments/proposals/halving_recursion.py and _results.md. | 60 |
| Modular-form / Hecke-trace coupling for π(x) via Σ_{p≤x} g(a_p(f)) (S60-fresh / crit, sketch only) | FAIL | C+E | DUPLICATE of "Modular forms approach | FAIL | C | Euler products need primes | 5" (Algebraic section), line 408 (Elliptic curve a_p as det entry — a_p defined only at primes, a_n composite needs factoring), line 739 (S60 Bessel-basis PSLQ closure on Selberg-trace shadows). Three orthogonal blockers: (1) Sato-Tate equidistribution on [-1,1] makes no fixed polynomial g identically 1 on a dense subset of {a_p(f) : p prime} — Weierstrass approximation goes the wrong way; degree-d L²-best-approximant residual on semicircle measure ≥ ½ − ½/π ≈ 0.34 for any finite d. (2) Family/CRT route reduces to evaluating a_n at composite n which requires factoring (sub-exponential, not polylog). (3) Trace-formula route extracts L-data, not π(x) — equivalent to L-function evaluation at known points. No experiment executed; closure follows from existing CLOSED_PATHS rows. Closes Proposal B4 (sketch). Critique cites: archive/ephemeral/critique_latest.md. | 60 |

# Closed Paths: Master Lookup (545+ Approaches)

**SEARCH THIS FILE before proposing any approach.** Use grep/ctrl-F.

Last updated: 2026-04-26 (Sessions 1-68 + S48-fresh + critique-46 + critique-56 + S57, 198+ sub-agents)

## Failure Modes
- **C** = Circularity (needs primes to compute primes)
- **E** = Equivalence (reduces to zeta zero sum / explicit formula)
- **I** = Information Loss (smooth approximation loses critical bits)

---

## Analytic / Explicit Formula / Zeta Zeros

| Approach | Verdict | Mode | Key Finding | Session |
|----------|---------|------|-------------|---------|
| Sparse matrix model for zeta zeros | FAIL | I | Tridiagonal Jacobi fits zeros with <0.05% error but uses 2N-1 params for N zeros (no compression). Off-diagonal entries b_i have 35% variation, no simple pattern. Toeplitz (N params) degrades at N=100. True extrapolation: 0.8-2.6% error. Information content not reduced. | 25 |
| Zeta-zero structure persists at N=2000 (S25 caveat resolved) | FAIL | I | Extension of S25 tests to N=2000. Pair-correlation RMS deviation from GUE *shrinks* from ~0.10 to 0.0864. PSLQ on never-tested LATE block γ_{1001..1100}: 0/1225 pairs, 0/4060 triples. Cross-block (early × late) PSLQ: 0/400. Discrepancy/Weyl ratios match N=1000. No structure emerges at 2x scale. See `experiments/analytic/zeta_structure/zeta_structure_n2000_results.md`. | 45 |
| 3-point correlation R_3(s_1,s_2) of zeta zeros | FAIL | I | First triple-correlation test on the project's data. Empirical R_3 vs GUE sine-kernel determinant ρ_3 = 1 − K(s_1)² − K(s_2−s_1)² − K(s_2)² + 2K(s_1)K(s_2−s_1)K(s_2) at N=2000 unfolded zeros: bulk RMS 0.0875 (n_ref=1995), diagonal slice (equally-spaced triples) RMS 0.0972, anti-diagonal (constant 2nd-3rd gap) RMS 0.0884. Third-cumulant rigidity test: c_3 of zero count in disjoint windows L∈{1,2,4,8,16,32} stays at ~10⁻³ for every L while Poisson predicts c_3 = L (factor 10⁴ separation at L=32). Closes the residual hypothesis "could match pair correlation while concealing higher-order cluster structure." See `experiments/analytic/zeta_structure/triple_correlation_results.md`. | 57 |
| Explicit formula partial sums recurrence | FAIL | I | No linear (r<=20), nonlinear (deg<=3), or difference recurrence. Residuals 2-6%. GUE phases make each term unpredictable from predecessors | 25 |
| Zeta zero pairwise rational relations | FAIL | I | 499,500 ratios tested; closest to p/q (q<=100) matches are no better than random (KS p=1.3e-6 but wrong direction — zeros FARTHER from rationals). GUE repulsion effect. | 25 |
| PSLQ linear relations among zeros | FAIL | I | 13,000+ tests at 60-digit precision: zero relations among subsets of 3-5 zeros with {1,pi,log(2pi)}. 1,225 pairwise tests negative. Large-K hits are lattice artifacts (random baseline confirms). Zeros linearly independent over Q. | 25 |
| DFT spectral structure of zeros | FAIL | I | Power spectrum matches GUE (corr=0.9999). Spectral flatness 0.93-0.999 at high freq (white noise). Pair correlation matches GUE 1-(sin(pi*r)/(pi*r))^2. Only faint p=2 signal (12x median). Number variance logarithmic (GUE). O(N) bits incompressible. | 25 |
| Zeta zeros mod constants (equidistribution) | FAIL | I | gamma_n mod m uniform for all 10 moduli tested (1, pi, log(2pi), 2pi, e, log(2,3,5,7)). KS p-values all >0.4. Weyl sums at 1/sqrt(N). Discrepancy BELOW random (GUE repulsion). Joint (mod 1, mod pi) independent. No arithmetic structure. | 25 |
| Convergence acceleration of zero sum | FAIL | I | Tested Richardson, Aitken Δ², Shanks, Padé, Cesàro, Euler-Maclaurin on partial zero sums for x=10^4..10^7. Errors GROW as N^{+1.0} (random walk). Best method (Shanks) gives O(1) improvement only. GUE-random phases make each term independent — no structured error to accelerate. | 32 |
| Self-correcting explicit formula + integer constraints | FAIL | I | Use fewer zeros + rounding/monotonicity/primality constraints. Truncation error is systematic bias ~O(N), not random noise. Constraints only help when error < 1, but error >> 1 with few zeros. Autocorr > 0.98. No triangulation possible. | 35,36 |
| Explicit formula proper convergence (mpmath R(x^ρ)) | FAIL | I | Naive R(x^ρ) summation DIVERGES: error grows from 3.5 (K=0) to 2076 (K=100) at x=10^4. Complex li branch cuts cause numerical instability. Only Lagarias-Odlyzko contour method is numerically stable. | 36 |
| Explicit formula + few zeros | FAIL | E | K^{-0.01} convergence | 5 |
| Explicit formula + 50 zeros | FAIL | I | More zeros can make WORSE | 6 |
| Explicit formula + 30 zeros | PARTIAL | E | 10% exact, best analytic | 10 |
| Weil explicit + Gaussian kernel | FAIL | I | Uncertainty principle: resolution * bandwidth >= const | 4 |
| Weil explicit + Beurling-Selberg | FAIL | I | Same uncertainty barrier | 4 |
| Mobius inversion of Pi(x) | PARTIAL | E | 10-30x better but still O(sqrt(x)/T) | 4 |
| Smooth zero sum integral | PARTIAL | E | Better than discrete but O(1) errors | 4 |
| Heuristic candidate generation + AKS | FAIL | I | Generate candidates near R^{-1}(n), filter with mod30/zeta/sieve. Candidates scale as n^0.577 (=sqrt(n)), not polylog. Interval width O(sqrt(p(n))*log(p(n))) is irreducible without computing zeta zero sum. With C=3.0 multiplier, 100% containment for n<=1000. Sieve reduces to ~4% of interval but still O(sqrt(n)) candidates. | 25 |
| Smoothed explicit + deconvolution | FAIL | I | Uncertainty principle blocks | 4 |
| Perron shifted contour (sigma>1) | FAIL | E | Numerically unstable, 20-40% error | 6 |
| Perron contour integral | FAIL | E | PROVEN equivalent to explicit formula | 5 |
| Cipolla Pade resummation | FAIL | E | Divergent, Pade can't generalize | 5 |
| Richardson/Aitken extrapolation | FAIL | E | No acceleration | 5 |
| Carlson's theorem | FAIL | E | Analytic continuation = explicit formula | 6 |
| Ramanujan-type series / Pade | FAIL | E | Cipolla DIVERGES, Pade gives 1372 mean error | 6 |
| Resurgent / trans-series | FAIL | E | Non-perturbative sectors ARE zeta zeros | 6 |
| Borel summation | FAIL | E | NOT APPLICABLE (power-law not factorial) | 6 |
| Riemann-Siegel analog | FAIL | E | = Lagarias-Odlyzko method | 6 |
| Zeta zero compression/FMM | FAIL | I | Spectral flatness 0.91, phase catastrophe | 9 |
| Connes-Weil quadratic form | FAIL | E | Finds zeros but can't sum them fast | 9 |
| Resummation (Borel/Pade/Shanks/Richardson/Mellin-Barnes) | FAIL | E | GUE statistics prevent partial sum prediction | 10 |
| FFT acceleration of explicit formula | FAIL | E | Constant factor only, not asymptotic | 7 |
| Gram points + Riemann-Siegel | PARTIAL | E | O(x^{1/2}*polylog) -- already known best | 8 |
| Analytic continuation (7 methods) | FAIL | E | Natural boundary at Re=0 | 8 |

  single-form attacks; composite-n a_n needs factoring.

  polylog-many evaluations of p at smaller inputs.

     the signal-side line 654 (S36 SVD result) into a joint dichotomy
     theorem on hierarchical compression of the explicit formula.

artefact and no new edge. The proposer's own self-assessment ("4 clean
negative closures with concrete structural reasons, but 0 novel
artifacts") is correct and is now reflected in CLOSED_PATHS.
